title: Area Of The Limit Curve For Symmetric Nonstationary Corner-Cutting Schemes
authors: Georgii Khoruzhevskii
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider corner-cutting schemes for closed oriented polygons in the plane. At each step every vertex is replaced by two points on the adjacent edges; the same cutting coefficient is used at all vertices of the current polygon, but this coefficient may vary from step to step. For such schemes we prove the existence of a continuous limit curve and derive an explicit formula for its oriented area. The main result separates two contributions: the geometry of the initial contour enters through its oriented area and a local sum of determinants built from neighboring edges, while the entire dependence on the refinement rule is contained in a single numerical constant. We also discuss the geometric meaning of this constant as an area arising in the standard angle. As applications we consider stationary de Rham curves, the Chaikin scheme, the connection with Archimedes' quadrature of the parabola, and special sequences of coefficients leading to a circle and to an arc of a hyperbola; these give corresponding series for [MATH] and [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies corner-cutting schemes for polygons, deriving an explicit formula for the oriented area of the limit curve.
motivation: To understand the geometric properties of limit curves generated by nonstationary corner-cutting schemes, separating contributions from initial geometry and refinement rule.
method: The authors analyze symmetric nonstationary corner-cutting schemes for closed oriented polygons, proving existence of a continuous limit curve and deriving an explicit area formula using determinants and a numerical constant.
result: The oriented area of the limit curve is expressed as a sum of the initial polygon's oriented area and a term involving a local sum of determinants, with the refinement rule's contribution captured by a single constant.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric interpretation of the constant and applies the result to stationary de Rham curves, Chaikin scheme, and special sequences leading to circles and hyperbolas, yielding series for π and √2.

title: On The Solution Of Kim, Pearcy And Shields Problem And Its Consequences
authors: Mubariz T. Garayev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a negative answer to a question due to Kim, Pearcy and Shields, namely, we prove that every nonscalar bounded linear operator on a Hilberts space [MATH] belongs to the class [MATH] defined in [56]. This gives an affirmative solution to the (hyper) invariant subspace problem in [MATH]. Our method of proof is based on Berezin symbol technique in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces.
tldr: The paper solves the (hyper)invariant subspace problem for Hilbert space operators using Berezin symbol techniques, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: To answer a question by Kim, Pearcy, and Shields regarding operator classes and the invariant subspace problem.
method: Uses Berezin symbol technique in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to prove that every nonscalar bounded linear operator belongs to a certain class.
result: Provides a negative answer to the Kim-Pearcy-Shields question and an affirmative solution to the (hyper)invariant subspace problem.
conclusion: The invariant subspace problem is resolved for Hilbert spaces using operator theory methods.

title: A Family Of Mixed-mixed Strongly Conservative Finite Element Methods For Biot's Model Of Consolidation
authors: Qingguo Hong, Johannes Kraus, Maria Lymbery
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a four-field formulation of Biot's quasi-static model of consolidation with the (effective) elastic stress, the solid displacement, the fluid flux and the fluid pressure as unknown physical quantities of interest. The weak form of this system composed of the momentum and mass balance equations complemented by the stress-strain relation and Darcy's law yields a two-fold perturbed saddle-point problem. Its well-posedness is proven for a natural choice of inifinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where the displacement-flux pair is sought in a novel Hilbert space. Next, based on recent works on [MATH]-conforming finite elements, we propose a family of mixed-mixed finite element methods that preserve the angular momentum as well as the fluid mass balance pointwise, i.e., in a strong sense. We prove the well-posedness of the arising discrete problem and establish optimal a priori error estimates for the related family of fully conservative mixed-mixed finite element methods.
tldr: This paper develops a family of mixed-mixed finite element methods for Biot's consolidation model, focusing on numerical analysis and conservation properties.
motivation: Biot's model of consolidation is important in geomechanics, and the goal is to design numerical methods that preserve angular momentum and fluid mass balance pointwise.
method: A four-field formulation is introduced, leading to a two-fold perturbed saddle-point problem. Using M-conforming finite elements, a family of mixed-mixed methods is proposed and analyzed.
result: Well-posedness of the discrete problem is proven, and optimal a priori error estimates are established for the family of fully conservative methods.
conclusion: The proposed methods achieve strong conservation properties and optimal convergence, making them suitable for simulating consolidation processes.

title: Convergence And Stability Of Truncated Euler-Maruyama Algorithm For Stochastic Proportional Delay Mckean-Vlasov Models With Jump Process
authors: Zhuoqi Liu Amr Abosenna
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic Mckean-Vlasov models have a substantial importance in different fields such as finance, biology and control. This paper puts the light on stochastic proportional delay Mckean-Vlasov model with L\'evy jump where the non-jump coefficients are granted the permission to grow beyond linearity. The truncated Euler-Maruyama algorithm is then applied to our addressed model where the convergence rate and almost sure exponential stability of the aforementioned numerical algorithm are being investigated. Finally, numerical examples are presented to foster the theoretical analysis done throughout the paper.
tldr: This paper studies the convergence and stability of a numerical algorithm for stochastic proportional delay McKean-Vlasov models with Lévy jumps.
motivation: Stochastic McKean-Vlasov models are important in finance, biology, and control, but numerical methods for such models with superlinear coefficients and jumps are not well understood.
method: The authors apply the truncated Euler-Maruyama algorithm to the stochastic proportional delay McKean-Vlasov model with Lévy jump, where non-jump coefficients can grow superlinearly, and analyze its convergence rate and almost sure exponential stability.
result: The paper establishes the convergence rate and almost sure exponential stability of the truncated Euler-Maruyama method for the considered model, supported by numerical examples.
conclusion: The truncated Euler-Maruyama algorithm is effective for simulating stochastic proportional delay McKean-Vlasov models with jumps and superlinear coefficients.

title: Finite Element Exponential Integration For Rough Solutions Of Nonlinear Wave Equations. Part I: Dirichlet Boundary Conditions On Polygonal And Polyhedral Domains
authors: Jiachuan Cao, Benjamin D\"orich, Marlis Hochbruck, Buyang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a fully discrete scheme for nonlinear wave equations on general bounded polygonal/polyhedral domains with initial data [MATH], [MATH], subject to the natural compatibility condition associated with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. The scheme combines an exponential Euler time integrator with a finite element spatial discretization. In contrast to existing low-regularity error analyses, which are mostly based on Fourier spectral discretizations, our approach applies to general bounded domains and finite element spatial discretizations. We prove rigorous error estimates for low-regularity solutions. The analysis is based on a frequency decomposition of the underlying elliptic operator, used solely as an analytical regularization device and not in the actual implementation, which allows low-regularity techniques to be extended beyond the Fourier spectral framework. The results also indicate that higher-order finite element methods remain advantageous in spatial approximation even for solutions of limited Sobolev regularity. Numerical experiments on different domains and with different polynomial degrees confirm the predicted convergence behavior.
tldr: This paper develops a finite element exponential integration method for nonlinear wave equations on polygonal/polyhedral domains with low-regularity solutions.
motivation: Existing low-regularity error analyses are mostly based on Fourier spectral discretizations, which are limited to simple domains. The authors aim to extend such techniques to general bounded domains using finite element methods.
method: The scheme combines an exponential Euler time integrator with finite element spatial discretization. A frequency decomposition of the elliptic operator is used as an analytical regularization device to enable low-regularity analysis beyond Fourier spectral frameworks.
result: Rigorous error estimates are proved for low-regularity solutions, showing that higher-order finite elements remain advantageous even for limited Sobolev regularity. Numerical experiments confirm predicted convergence.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a robust numerical scheme for nonlinear wave equations on complex domains with rough initial data, extending low-regularity techniques to finite element discretizations.

title: Batteriesandthe BritishEnergy System
authors: Waqquas Bukhsh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Batteries are becoming a central part of modern energy systems, especially as electricity, transport and heat are decarbonised. In Great Britain, batteries already play an important role by providing flexibility and acting as a buffer for the system, and their importance will continue to grow as the system moves towards net zero by 2050. title: End-to-End Supply Chain Planning In The Paper Industry Via Column Generation And Benders Decomposition
authors: Changkun Guan, Amira Hijazi, Pascal van Hentenryck
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Problem definition: The paper studies an integrated end-to-end planning problem in large-scale paper manufacturing, where production scheduling, trimming decisions, vehicle loading, and multi-period fulfillment of make-to-order and make-to-stock demand must be coordinated over time. In practice, these decisions are often optimized sequentially, leading to material waste, inefficient transportation, and degraded service levels. Solving the fully integrated problem at industrial scale remains computationally challenging due to its combinatorial structure. Methodology/results: A key structural feature of the problem is that downstream fulfillment decisions depend on upstream production and logistics choices only through aggregate supply availability over time. By exploiting this structure, the paper develops an exact mathematical formulation and proposes a two-phase hybrid framework (BDCG-DP) that integrates column generation (CG) using exact dynamic-programming (DP) for supply-side decisions with Benders decomposition (BD) for downstream fulfillment. Computational experiments on proprietary instances from a major North American paper manufacturer show that BDCG-DP lowers total costs by 24.4% compared to a traditional CG-DP on challenging eight-week planning problems. Median runtime for four-week planning problems decreases from over five hours using CG-DP to under one hour using BDCG-DP. Managerial implications: This paper provides the first exact model that integrates production, trimming, load planning, and multi-period fulfillment at an industrial scale. The proposed approach returns integer-feasible plans within 2.3 to 6 hours for the most complex planning problems, enabling planners to access high-quality implementable schedules within hours, a capability that was previously unavailable in practice.
tldr: This paper presents an exact optimization framework for integrated supply chain planning in the paper industry, combining column generation and Benders decomposition.
motivation: Sequential optimization of production, trimming, loading, and fulfillment leads to waste and inefficiency; an integrated solution is needed but computationally challenging.
method: The authors propose a two-phase hybrid framework (BDCG-DP) that uses column generation with dynamic programming for supply-side decisions and Benders decomposition for downstream fulfillment.
result: On industrial instances, BDCG-DP reduces total costs by 24.4% and cuts median runtime from over 5 hours to under 1 hour for four-week planning problems.
conclusion: The framework provides the first exact, scalable solution for end-to-end planning in paper manufacturing, enabling high-quality implementable schedules within hours.

title: Augmented Lagrangian Preconditioning For A Simplified Ericksen--Leslie Model Of Nematic Liquid Crystals
authors: Yanying Li, Xu Qian, Jingmin Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numerical solution of the simplified Ericksen--Leslie model for nematic liquid crystals is challenging because the flow and director equations are strongly coupled and because incompressibility and the unit-length condition must be enforced simultaneously. A Lagrange multiplier formulation avoids a small Ginzburg--Landau parameter, but the Newton systems have a double saddle-point structure. We develop an augmented Lagrangian block preconditioner in which both constraints are augmented while their discrete enforcement remains multiplier based. After finite element discretization and backward Euler time integration, the Newton increments are grouped into velocity--director and pressure-multiplier variables. A block-diagonal approximation of the coupled velocity-director block then leads to separate, physically scaled approximations of the pressure and director-multiplier Schur complements. Manufactured-solution tests show the expected spatial accuracy and first-order temporal convergence for the primary variables; the multiplier error reaches a spatial-error floor on the fixed mesh used in the temporal study. In the reported parameter ranges, the outer FGMRES iteration counts are nearly mesh independent, remain stable under time-step and viscosity variation, and improve as the augmentation parameters increase. A smooth benchmark also exhibits monotone decay of the computed total energy.
tldr: This paper develops an augmented Lagrangian preconditioner for the numerical simulation of nematic liquid crystals using a simplified Ericksen-Leslie model.
motivation: Solving the simplified Ericksen-Leslie model is challenging due to strong coupling and simultaneous enforcement of incompressibility and unit-length constraints; efficient preconditioners are needed.
method: An augmented Lagrangian block preconditioner is developed for the double saddle-point Newton systems arising from finite element discretization and backward Euler time integration, with block-diagonal approximations for the coupled velocity-director block.
result: Manufactured-solution tests confirm expected spatial accuracy and first-order temporal convergence; outer FGMRES iteration counts are nearly mesh independent and stable under parameter variation.
conclusion: The proposed preconditioner effectively handles the constraints and yields robust iterative solver performance for this liquid crystal model.

title: De-floored Principal Component Regression: When Rank Selection Alone Is Insufficient For Prediction
authors: Peng Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Principal component regression (PCR) regularizes high-dimensional prediction by choosing a spectral cutoff, but rank selection cannot correct systematic inflation of the retained empirical eigenvalues. We study clean Gaussian random designs in which the aggregate covariance tail creates a nearly scalar sample-space floor comparable to the predictive head scale. De-floored principal component regression (dPCR) retains the cutoff and subtracts an estimated floor from the retained denominators. We prove an ordinary-PCR prediction-risk lower bound uniform over all ranks and a high-probability dPCR upper bound. When the floor is sharp and inexpensive to remove in population prediction risk, the conditional risk of dPCR is asymptotically negligible relative to that of the best ordinary PCR rank. An exact risk decomposition explains the separation: denominator inflation is governed by first spectral mass, whereas the clean prediction cost of correction is governed by squared spectral mass. A same-sample trimmed-mean floor estimate attains the oracle dPCR upper-bound rate at a prespecified rank, and the separation persists under approximate predictive alignment when the tail prediction-energy fraction vanishes. Separate pointwise fixed-aspect formulas show that the risk-optimal positive scalar correction improves rank-[MATH] PCR, whereas mean-floor subtraction is generally not optimal for a broad Marchenko--Pastur bulk.
tldr: This paper proposes a de-floored principal component regression method to correct eigenvalue inflation in high-dimensional prediction.
motivation: Standard principal component regression suffers from systematic inflation of empirical eigenvalues, which degrades prediction performance.
method: The authors propose subtracting an estimated floor from retained eigenvalues and provide theoretical risk bounds under Gaussian random designs.
result: De-floored PCR achieves asymptotically negligible conditional risk relative to the best ordinary PCR rank, with a separation governed by spectral mass.
conclusion: The proposed correction improves prediction risk, but the optimal correction is not simply mean-floor subtraction for broad spectral bulks.

title: A Deep Second-Order Stochastic Residual Method For Fully Nonlinear Parabolic PDEs
authors: Jihao Long Zhenhua Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Deep Second-Order Stochastic Residual Method (D2SRM) for high-dimensional, Hessian-dependent fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs. A single scalar space--time network generates derivative-consistent approximations of the solution, gradient, and Hessian, which are trained jointly through second-order Brownian one-step residuals and terminal value and gradient penalties. For globally Lipschitz equations with identity diffusion and sufficiently weak Hessian coupling, we establish well-posedness in a Brownian occupation space and develop a population-level convergence theory. Under additional regularity, an a posteriori estimate bounds the squared full-jet occupation error of any admissible candidate by the time step and its population objective. For approximate population minimizers, the error bound separates time discretization, neural approximation, and population suboptimality; when the latter two terms are [MATH], the full-jet occupation norm is [MATH]. Experiments on a 100-dimensional manufactured benchmark compare terminal treatments, probe Hessian couplings inside and outside the proved small-gain range, and show decreasing errors as the time step decreases. The code is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper introduces a deep learning method for solving high-dimensional fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs using second-order stochastic residuals.
motivation: High-dimensional fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs are challenging to solve numerically, and existing methods often struggle with Hessian-dependent terms.
method: The D2SRM uses a single scalar space-time neural network to approximate the solution, gradient, and Hessian, trained jointly via second-order Brownian one-step residuals and terminal penalties.
result: The method achieves well-posedness in a Brownian occupation space, provides a posteriori error bounds, and demonstrates decreasing errors with smaller time steps on a 100-dimensional benchmark.
conclusion: D2SRM offers a promising approach for high-dimensional PDEs, but the paper focuses on numerical analysis and machine learning, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Power Set Of A Quasinilpotent Backward Weighted Shift
authors: Egor Ignatev

Yang associated with each nonzero vector [MATH] the local resolvent-growth exponent [MATH], and introduced the power set [MATH]. tldr: This paper studies the power set of a quasinilpotent backward weighted shift operator on a Banach space, proving bounds on local resolvent-growth exponents.
motivation: To answer open questions about the power set of quasinilpotent operators and to weaken hypotheses for backward weighted shifts.
method: Analytic operator theory techniques, including spectral analysis and properties of weighted shifts.
result: Proves that the power set is contained in [0,1] for any quasinilpotent operator, and that it equals [0,1] for strictly decreasing ℓ^p-summable weight sequences.
conclusion: The results settle a question by Ji and Zhang and improve upon previous work by Hu and Ji.

title: Analytic Regularity For A Fourth-order Singularly Perturbed Boundary Balue Problem With Two Small Parameters
authors: C. Xenophontos I. Sykopetritou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a fourth order singularly perturbed boundary value problem with two small parameters, in one dimension, under the assumption of analytic input data. We show that the solution may be decomposed into a smooth part, two different width boundary layers, and a negligible remainder. We provide estimates for arbitrary order derivatives of each term of the decomposition, which are explicit in the differentiation order and the singular perturbation parameters, and are needed for proving the convergence of high order numerical methods, such as the [MATH] versions of the Finite Element Method. We also provide classical differentiability results, which show that the solution will be analytic, if the data are analytic, but negative powers of the singular perturbation parameter(s) show up once we start differentiating.
tldr: This paper analyzes the analytic regularity of a fourth-order singularly perturbed boundary value problem with two small parameters, providing derivative estimates for numerical methods.
motivation: To understand the solution structure and regularity of a singularly perturbed problem with two parameters, which is essential for developing high-order numerical methods.
method: The solution is decomposed into a smooth part, two boundary layers, and a remainder; estimates for arbitrary order derivatives are derived using analytic function theory.
result: Explicit derivative bounds are obtained, showing analyticity of the solution with negative powers of the perturbation parameters upon differentiation.
conclusion: The results provide the necessary regularity estimates for convergence proofs of high-order finite element methods for this class of problems.

title: Benchmarking Optimization Algorithms With Quality Profiles And Test Set Profiles
authors: G. Fasano, C. Piermarini, M. Roma
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a couple of novel tools for benchmarking optimization algorithms which possibly converge to different solutions on a test set: the quality profiles and the test set profiles. Their aim is to assess and compare algorithms in terms of quality (i.e. value of the objective function) of the obtained solutions, as well as to assess the consistency of the test set. A key distinguishing feature of the quality profiles we propose is its comparative deterministic procedure that emphasizes the accuracy of the solution, rather than the computational burden of solvers. In this regard, several test set--dependent approaches for both comparing and ranking algorithms have already been proposed in the literature, representing widely used benchmarking procedures. We believe that the joint use of such procedures, along with the novel quality profiles detailed here, should enhance the benchmarking process, in all those cases where the comparison encompasses exact methods as well as heuristics. Moreover, the literature on numerical optimization seems to have paid less attention, in the last decade, to determining how appropriate a test set used for benchmarking the selected solvers may be. This motivates the introduction of test set profiles, which assess the appropriateness of a test set and represent the flip side of evaluating the robustness of the solvers on that test set. This paper also includes extensive numerical experiments, showing the usefulness of quality profiles in both smooth and nonsmooth (derivative--free) optimization, along with the reference to a MATLAB code for plotting quality profiles and test set profiles.
tldr: This paper proposes quality profiles and test set profiles for benchmarking optimization algorithms, focusing on solution accuracy rather than computational cost.
motivation: Existing benchmarking tools often emphasize computational burden; the authors aim to provide a deterministic comparative procedure that highlights solution quality and assess test set appropriateness.
method: The authors introduce quality profiles, which compare algorithms based on the objective function value of obtained solutions, and test set profiles to evaluate the consistency of the test set. They provide a MATLAB implementation and test on smooth and nonsmooth optimization problems.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the usefulness of quality profiles in both smooth and derivative-free optimization, and test set profiles help assess test set appropriateness.
conclusion: The proposed profiles enhance benchmarking by focusing on solution accuracy and test set consistency, complementing existing procedures.

title: Linearization Problem For A System Of Two Second-Order ODEs Via Cartan's Method: Branch I
authors: Batoul M. Raddad, Ahmad Y. Al-Dweik, Marwan Aloqeili, F. M. Mahomed
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cartan's method classifies the class of linearizable system of two second-order ODEs into many branches. This paper investigates Branch I of the classification, characterized by a rank-one generalized Wilczynski invariant matrix and the vanishing of two relative invariants [MATH] and [MATH]. It is demonstrated that any linearizable system belonging to this branch admits an eight-dimensional Lie point symmetry algebra. The canonical form for this class is provided and the invariant characterizations based on the obtained rank-zero invariant coframe and the corresponding constant structure equations are established. Also, a systematic procedure for constructing the linearizing point transformation is derived. The theoretical results are illustrated by several examples.
tldr: This paper applies Cartan's method to classify linearizable systems of two second-order ODEs in Branch I, providing canonical forms and symmetry algebras.
motivation: The study aims to complete the classification of linearizable systems of two second-order ODEs using Cartan's geometric approach, focusing on Branch I characterized by specific invariant conditions.
method: Cartan's method of equivalence is used to derive invariant characterizations, including a rank-zero invariant coframe and constant structure equations, leading to the identification of an eight-dimensional Lie point symmetry algebra.
result: The paper provides the canonical form for Branch I linearizable systems and a systematic procedure for constructing the linearizing point transformation, illustrated with examples.
conclusion: The work completes the classification for Branch I, offering a clear geometric characterization and practical transformation method for such ODE systems.

title: Duality In Biperiodic Fibonacci Words Substitution Frequencies And Combinatorial Invariants
authors: Jasem Hamoud
abstract: ArXiv:2607.16844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a natural duality on the family of biperiodic Fibonacci words [MATH] generated by the directive sequence [MATH]. Both of [MATH] and [MATH] are related by the explicit morphism [MATH], [MATH], establishing a precise substitutional correspondence between them. We compute the exact letter frequencies, give a complete description of the return words for each letter, prove the existence of arbitrarily long palindromic prefixes, and determine the continued fraction expansion of the slope [MATH]. These findings reveal that the apparent asymmetry in several invariants arises uniformly from the length-redistribution mechanism induced by the morphism [MATH].
